subject: Immediate: siren3b elevated 503/timeouts — customer impact and mitigation
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-18T09:12:00Z
Subject: Immediate: siren3b elevated 503/timeouts — customer impact and mitigation

Hi Lindsey / Sanjay —

We’re seeing an elevated rate of 503s and timeouts from model siren3b serving in us-east-1 beginning ~08:50 UTC. Early telemetry indicates errors are concentrated on long-context streaming requests and a small subset of hosts are returning transient 5xx.

What we’ve done so far:
- Scoped impact: ~3% of your inference calls (60m window) returned 5xx or timed out; we’ve attached a short log snippet and an impact graph.
- Failover: we’ve configured routing to prefer siren3b-int8 (quantized variant) for new requests and enabled automatic fallback to siren2b for critical routes.
- Ops actions: engineering is patching a kernel-selection regression; we opened incident #7421 in ops.

Immediate asks for Atlas Health:
1) Confirm whether you can tolerate the temporary quality delta from siren3b-int8 / siren2b for high-volume endpoints during remediation.
2) If you have a strict SLA window for any specific route, flag it and we’ll keep it on dedicated capacity.

I’ll provide an hourly update until resolved. Apologies for the disruption — we know this is impacting your users and are prioritizing rollback and stability.

Thanks,
Neha
Neha Kapoor
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Immediate: siren3b elevated 503/timeouts — customer impact and mitigation

Lindsey — quick technical update and plan: 

Root cause (initial triage): a recent kernel-selection change in the inference runtime can cause a suboptimal memory layout for long-sequence attention, which increases KV-cache memory pressure and triggers intermittent OOMs on a small subset of hosts. That in turn results in 5xx and request cancellation.

Work we’re doing now (in parallel):
- Short term (next 30–90m): roll traffic away from the affected pool to siren3b-int8 and siren2b; increase autoscale headroom on Dedicated pools serving Atlas routes; apply a conservative kernel-selection rollback on the affected hosts.
- Medium term (24–72h): patch the kernel-selection heuristic, add integration tests for long-context KV memory patterns, and harden OOM detection to trigger local request rerouting before returning 5xx.
- Communication: we’ll post updates to https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/7421 and flag customer-specific follow-ups.

ETA: we expect visible reduction in 5xx within ~45 minutes from now; a full restoration to baseline within 3–6 hours depending on capacity warm-up. If you cannot accept the small quality delta from siren3b-int8, we will pin your critical routes to a siren2b pool on Dedicated capacity for the next 12h while we finish the rollback.

Ben — can you take ownership on the commercial ask for credits / SLA exceptions if Atlas requests?

Aditya
Sr. Engineering Manager, Runtime

Date: 2027-04-20T17:30:00Z
Subject: Postmortem: siren3b elevated 5xx/timeouts (us-east-1) — resolution and next steps

Hi Lindsey / Sanjay —

Thanks again for your patience while we investigated and remediated the siren3b incident. Below is a brief postmortem and the actions we’ve taken. I’ve attached the full postmortem doc as well.

Summary:
- Incident window: 2027-04-18 08:50 UTC — 2027-04-18 13:10 UTC (primary impact); residual rate tracked into 2027-04-19 as small edge cases.
- Impact: ~3% of Atlas Health inference calls returned 5xx/timeouts during the peak window. No data loss; requests either failed fast or fell back to siren3b-int8 / siren2b variants.
- Root cause: a kernel-selection heuristic introduced in release r2027.04.12 could choose kernels that increase KV-cache memory usage for long-attention contexts, pushing some hosts into OOM and causing request cancellations (5xx).

Resolved actions taken:
1) Rollback: reverted kernel-selection change on affected pools (completed 2027-04-18 11:05 UTC).
2) Routing: temporarily routed Atlas-critical traffic to siren3b-int8 and pinned high-priority routes to siren2b dedicated pool until autoscale warmed (completed 2027-04-18 12:30 UTC).
3) Monitoring: added an alert and dashboard for KV-cache growth per host and an automatic local-reroute on OOM candidate events.
4) Testing: expanded long-context integration tests in CI and added a memory-pressure scenario to nightly regression runs.
5) Customer relief: Ben will follow up on credits/SLA accommodation; if you’d like, we can propose a formal one-off credit in the next 48 hours.

Next steps (owner / ETA):
- Aditya / Runtime: shipping a safe kernel-selection patch and full unit/integration tests by 2027-04-22.
- Platform Reliability: finalize autoscale warm-up improvements and a canary path for kernel changes (2027-04-29).
- Neha / Customer Ops: coordinate a 1:1 review with your engineering leads to walk the postmortem and confirm whether the temporary routing had any notable customer-visible regressions (week of 2027-04-26).

We’re closing incident #7421 but keeping the postmortem doc open for comments; link: https://drive.redwood.ai/open?id=1A2B3C-siren3b-postmortem.

Apologies again for the disruption — we treat availability regressions like this very seriously and will make sure the corrective actions reduce the likelihood of recurrence.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
